samples.text:
The diagram shows how the seawater is changed into drinking water in a desalination plant. There are eight steps in the process.

Firstly, seawater is drawn in through a pipe which have a screen. Then in the pre-treatment stage, sand filters remove particles and algae from the water. After that a high-pressure pump pressurise the water to about 60 bar.

Next, the water goes to reverse osmosis. In this stage, membranes separates the fresh water and the salt. The salty waste, which is called brine, is diluted and it is returned to the sea. The fresh water continue to the next stage.

After that, calcium and magnesium are added to the water, this is remineralisation. Then a small amount of chlorine is added for disinfection. Finally, the water is stored in a reservoir and then it is piped to homes.

Overall, the process is linear and it starts with seawater and ends with drinking water for homes. The main stage is reverse osmosis because it takes the salt out.
samples.why: Overview present but late and simple · all eight stages covered in sequence · mechanical linking · adequate vocabulary with repetition · several agreement errors and a comma splice that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram illustrates the process of producing drinking water from seawater at a desalination plant.

Overall, there are eight stages in this linear process, starting with the intake of seawater and ending with the supply of drinking water to homes. The key stage is reverse osmosis, where salt is removed, and this also produces a waste product that is returned to the sea.

Initially, seawater is drawn in through a screened pipe and passes through sand filters, which remove particles and algae. The water is then pressurised to about 60 bar by a high-pressure pump before it is forced into the reverse osmosis unit. Here, membranes separate the fresh water from the salt.

At this point, the salty waste, known as brine, is diluted and discharged back into the sea. Meanwhile, the fresh water undergoes remineralisation, in which calcium and magnesium is added. After that, it is disinfected with a small amount of chlorine. In final stage, the treated water is kept in a reservoir and later piped to households, where it can be used for drinking.
samples.why: Clear overview naming the key stage · logical progression with passive forms and varied linkers · less common vocabulary (discharged, undergoes) · mostly error-free with two minor slips.

samples.text:
The diagram explains how seawater is converted into potable water at a desalination facility.

In essence, the treatment follows eight consecutive stages, from the intake of raw seawater to the delivery of drinking water to homes. At the heart of the process lies reverse osmosis, which splits the flow into fresh water for further treatment and salty waste that is discharged.

To begin with, seawater is drawn into the plant through a screened pipe, after which it is pre-treated using sand filters that trap particles and algae. A high-pressure pump then raises the pressure of the water to approximately 60 bar, enabling it to pass through reverse osmosis membranes, where the fresh water is separated from the salt.

The resulting salty waste is diluted and returned to the sea. The desalinated water, by contrast, is remineralised through the addition of calcium and magnesium, before being disinfected with a small quantity of chlorine. Finally, the treated water is held in a storage reservoir, from which it is piped to residential properties, completing its transformation from seawater into a safe supply for household consumption.
samples.why: Precise overview identifying the pivotal stage and its two outputs · every stage covered fluently · wide, accurate vocabulary (potable, remineralised) · sophisticated passive and relative structures · error-free.
